title: Minimax Optimal-Value Risk with Two Response Archetypes and a Concealed Category Map
banked_reason: Math and rubric PASS, but incremental below field: structural restrictions and missing growing-intensity original-record sharp theorem/computational usability constrain paper_score_ceiling to 5.8 < 7.4.
gap_reasons: The delivered contribution is an exact scalar-amplitude decision benchmark under complementary profiles, known center, known uniform masses and fair treatment; its structural restrictions keep it below field significance despite the completed continuum analysis.

It does not settle the broader unknown-grouping problem raised in [Zeng et al.'s discussion](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.00118v3), and the internal predecessor comparisons remain unpublished, unverified priority claims rather than grounds for rejecting novelty.
The framing accurately distinguishes minimax scalar reduction from full-vector sufficiency and the Poisson endpoint from original-record limits, so there is no stale sharpness overclaim.

Sharp original-record attainment covers compact positive intensities, whereas λR*(λ)→κ is established only for the Poisson experiment; a sharp original-record constant across the growing-intensity inference-versus-learning separation remains undelivered.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery completed the scalar reduction, compact-intensity original-record birthday theorem, continuum certificates, endpoint localization and approximate-balance robustness; both math/rubric reviews passed after four cited-source attestations. The mathematical kernel did not collapse, but the final contribution was capped at incremental for restricted scope and incomplete computational usability. No formalization was started; a re-raise requires a growing-intensity sharp original-record theorem and stronger computational evidence.
tldr: The complete original-record minimax optimal-value risk converges, with quantitative reconstruction and attaining decisions, to a certified continuum birthday-Poisson curve. The benchmark has known uniform categories, fair randomized treatment, binary outcomes, a known response center, and two unknown complementary response archetypes with an exactly balanced concealed category map. At \(n/\sqrt d\to\lambda>0\), permutation reduction precedes the comparison of experiments. Retaining all three arm-marked channels and then signed pooling gives an exact scalar minimax game. In the same class, value MSE has order \(\min\{1,\sqrt d/n\}\), while policy regret has order \(\min\{1,\sqrt{d/n}\}\); consistency consequently requires \(n/\sqrt d\to\infty\) and \(n/d\to\infty\), respectively. Finite programs certify the entire curve, including an informative intensity-one value. Its small-intensity expansion has an explicit remainder, and its large-intensity endpoint is the globally localized Gaussian-root constant \(\lambda R^\star(\lambda)\to\kappa\), with data-only attaining Poisson decisions and arbitrary-accuracy finite certificates for \(\kappa\). Approximate-balance robustness distinguishes full-experiment stability under \(\beta\sqrt n\to0\) from tolerance-class value-curve stability under \(\beta\to0\).
gap: Zeng et al. raises unknown equal-mean grouping in discrete causal inference. Existing norm rates, permutation-mixture bounds and internal marked-Poisson examples leave the complete continuum optimal-value decision curve with quantitative original-record attainment unresolved in this particular sparse categorical benchmark.
fill: The original-record birthday theorem is the headline. Certified finite decision programs characterize \(R^\star(\lambda)\), with an informative nonzero calibration, endpoint analyses and total data-only attaining procedures. Matched value-MSE and policy-regret boundaries use the identical balanced class. The approximate-balance theorem adds explicit experiment and welfare-risk error budgets, while the singleton diagnostic identifies the information omitted outside the balanced-experiment regime.
